records.name: First World Travel Network
records.summary: Baseline overland and maritime travel assumptions for the authored first world, now resolved through pixel-based route geometry on the shared world map grid.

modeProfiles.name: On Foot
modeProfiles.notes: Represents ordinary laden travel on maintained routes at about 30 km per day before terrain and feature modifiers.

modeProfiles.name: Mounted
modeProfiles.notes: Represents relay riding, mounted messengers, and light pack riders averaging about 60 km per day before modifiers.

modeProfiles.name: Wagon
modeProfiles.notes: Represents animal-drawn land vehicles and freight wagons averaging about 40 km per day on workable roads.

modeProfiles.name: River Barge
modeProfiles.notes: Represents barges, tow craft, and canal freight moving about 120 km per day on navigable inland water.

modeProfiles.name: Coastal Ship
modeProfiles.notes: Represents ordinary coastal sail making about 200 km per day in fair conditions while hugging known shores and island chains.

modeProfiles.name: Bluewater Ship
modeProfiles.notes: Represents long-range sea sail with the same fair-weather pace as coastal shipping but greater endurance across exposed open-water lanes.

travelBenchmarks.summary: Reference marching pace for ordinary overland travel at about 30 km per day.
Reference mounted pace for horse relays, couriers, and light rider caravans at about 60 km per day.
Reference sailing pace for ordinary medieval-scale shipping at about 200 km per day.

terrainVarianceRules.name: Open Plains
terrainVarianceRules.summary: Long sightlines and gentle grades favor riders, wagons, and marching columns.

terrainVarianceRules.name: Temperate Farmland
terrainVarianceRules.summary: Cultivated lowlands support the most consistent overland travel in settled regions.

terrainVarianceRules.name: Deep Forest
terrainVarianceRules.summary: Dense cover, roots, and wet ground punish anything wider than a trail column.

terrainVarianceRules.name: Marshland
terrainVarianceRules.summary: Sodden ground, channels, and insects make marsh crossings slow and unreliable.

terrainVarianceRules.name: Upland Hills
terrainVarianceRules.summary: Broken grades and stream cuts slow freight and mounted movement more than marching infantry.

terrainVarianceRules.name: Mountain Pass
terrainVarianceRules.summary: Switchbacks, thin ledges, and snow risks turn mountain transit into a controlled bottleneck.

terrainVarianceRules.name: Desert Plateau
terrainVarianceRules.summary: Heat, water discipline, and sparse shade reduce sustained pace even on otherwise open ground.

terrainVarianceRules.name: Navigable River
terrainVarianceRules.summary: Reliable current and draft depth make rivers the fastest bulk-movement corridors inland.

terrainVarianceRules.name: Open Sea
terrainVarianceRules.summary: Fair-weather sea travel holds to baseline sailing pace but remains weather-sensitive.

terrainVarianceRules.name: Storm Belt
terrainVarianceRules.summary: Persistent squalls and swells impose severe time uncertainty on exposed sea lanes.

featureVarianceRules.name: Paved Road
featureVarianceRules.summary: Engineered roads reduce attrition and improve reliable travel speed for all land traffic.

featureVarianceRules.name: River Crossing
featureVarianceRules.summary: Unbridged crossings delay caravans and introduce waiting time for ferries or fords.

featureVarianceRules.name: Bridge or Ferry Control Point
featureVarianceRules.summary: Bridgeheads and managed ferry slips reduce crossing chaos but still impose toll and queue friction.

featureVarianceRules.name: Mountain Switchbacks
featureVarianceRules.summary: Cut roads and cliff turns preserve access but slow any heavy overland movement.

featureVarianceRules.name: Canal Lock
featureVarianceRules.summary: Locks improve navigability across elevation changes but add handling delays at each chamber.

featureVarianceRules.name: Drydock Refit
featureVarianceRules.summary: Large ports can service hulls and crews quickly, but major refits still insert planned delay.

featureVarianceRules.name: Favorable Current
featureVarianceRules.summary: Current and seasonal winds shorten trips on aligned river and coastal segments.

featureVarianceRules.name: Bad Weather
featureVarianceRules.summary: Mud, storms, and visibility loss broaden travel uncertainty across all route types.

routeRecords.name: Aurelis-Vinecross Road
routeRecords.notes: A heavily worked farm-road and cask route linking the southern capital to its inland viticulture market.

routeRecords.name: Aurelis-Stonevein Crown Track
routeRecords.notes: Ore caravans and crown wagons use this route to connect Kaelvar's southern court with the dwarf-held upland mines.

routeRecords.name: Brineharbor-Aurelis Coastal Run
routeRecords.notes: Salt fish, pearls, and northern cargoes move south along the safer Kaelvar littoral instead of crossing the open ocean.

routeRecords.name: Highcrown-Blueflow River Corridor
routeRecords.notes: This is one of Valtherion's core administrative corridors, with the river doing most of the heavy freight work.

routeRecords.name: Riverthrone-Granary Crown Grainwater
routeRecords.notes: Draemor's grain core relies on both lock-managed river movement and dense road traffic into the capital basin.

routeRecords.name: Seabanner-Tidecrown Coastway
routeRecords.notes: Short-haul shipping keeps Serathyl's main naval harbor fed with timber, fish, and citrus from nearby coast towns.

routeRecords.name: Sunspire Reach-Silvermere Valley Road
routeRecords.notes: The main civilized road through Talmyra's northern valleys, carrying food, guards, and frontier administrators.

routeRecords.name: Spicehook-Watcher's Gate Frontier Road
routeRecords.notes: Convoys moving between Talmyra's spice coast and its eastern cliff fortresses accept high delay variance due to weather and ground.

routeRecords.name: Starfall Port-Harbormast Quay Island Run
routeRecords.notes: A high-frequency convoy leg inside the Myridian Chain, used by bonded warehouses and naval patrols.

routeRecords.name: Breaksail-Riverthrone Gulf Road
routeRecords.notes: The main overland backup route between Draemor's capital basin and its southern sea outlet.

routeRecords.name: Redcliff Quay-Brineharbor Coast Roadstead
routeRecords.notes: This north-south Kaelvar lane links the royal coast to the salt and fish harbors of the Shattercap Isles.

routeRecords.name: Lantern Key-Driftglass Outpost Patrol Run
routeRecords.notes: Short-haul cutters from Lantern Key resupply the outer watch post whenever weather allows.

interPortShipRoutes.name: Brineharbor-Starfall Northern Lane
interPortShipRoutes.notes: A northern island-hopping lane linking Kaelvar's outer harbors to the Myridian naval hub.

interPortShipRoutes.name: Starfall-Blueflow Merchant Lane
interPortShipRoutes.notes: The main northern merchant corridor from the Myridian hub to Valtherion's eastern river ports.

interPortShipRoutes.name: Aurelis-Seabanner Gulf Lane
interPortShipRoutes.notes: A sheltered but still weather-sensitive gulf lane between Kaelvar's southern capital and Serathyl's merchant coast.

interPortShipRoutes.name: Seabanner-Breaksail Inner Sea Lane
interPortShipRoutes.notes: A dense regional sea lane for grain, timber, fish, and finished goods between Serathyl and Draemor.

interPortShipRoutes.name: Breaksail-Lantern Central Crossing
interPortShipRoutes.notes: A central-ocean crossing that links Draemor's southern ports to the Lantern Isles trading cluster.

interPortShipRoutes.name: Lantern-Stormfang Southern Reach
interPortShipRoutes.notes: A long bluewater approach that runs into the rough southern seas near the Serpent's Wake.

interPortShipRoutes.name: Breaksail-Saltfang Southern Trade Lane
interPortShipRoutes.notes: The main southern lane for moving grain northbound and spices or hardwoods westbound between Draemor and Talmyra.

interPortShipRoutes.name: Stormfang-Aurora Far East Lane
interPortShipRoutes.notes: A hard bluewater lane linking the storm arc to the polar whaling and pearl approaches of Dawnreach.
